original.description: Profile LOCAL-006 flagged that depositFor on the price-scaled copy makes 3 external calls per user per loop iteration (dispatcherHook.pull() via _syncBudget, plus nftMinter.configs() + dispatcherHook.mintDebt() via the tail _recomputeSchedule) versus 1 storage-only recompute on the depletion copy, and warned that migrateIn slices must be 'substantially smaller'. MEASURED: the premium is 1.27x, not an order of magnitude, and there is NO realistic DoS ceiling.

original.verdict: REFUTED as a DoS. The real BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.pull() is a no-op after the first iteration of a loop (mintDebt is zeroed on the first pull), so the mock is representative; allow ~1.5x headroom for the real hook's nonReentrant + guard and for calldata.

dispositions.reason: VERIFIED CLEAN — no finding. original.type: operator footgun / availability - hook recipient wiring
original.description: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.pull() is onlyOwnerOrRecipient and additionally reverts RecipientUnset when recipient == address(0). The staker calls dispatcherHook.pull() with msg.sender == itself, so a staker wired to a hook on which it is NOT the recipient reverts on EVERY _syncBudget path - stake, unstake, claim, depositFor, initiateMigration, pullAndRefresh - unconditionally, even when mintDebt is zero. In a cross-staker migration the target staker is by construction not yet the hook's recipient, so wiring its dispatcherHook before flipping hook.setRecipient bricks the entire migration at the first depositFor. The in-repo orchestrator tests never wire a real (or recipient-guarded) hook to the target, so this ordering constraint is untested and undocumented.
original.economicImpact: Availability only - no value at risk. emergencyWithdraw and userMigrate never call pull(), so principal always escapes.
original.attackScenario: Operator sequence: deploy new staker -> setDispatcherHook(sharedHook) -> setMigrator -> migrate(users). The batchMigrate leg succeeds (no _syncBudget), then depositFor reverts OnlyOwnerOrRecipient with the batch's ERC1155 already pulled into the migrator - a partially-executed migration.
original.recommendation: Runbook: either leave the target's dispatcherHook unset until hook.setRecipient(target) has landed, or flip the recipient first. Note the reciprocal hazard: once the recipient is flipped, the SOURCE staker's stake/unstake/claim/pullAndRefresh brick too (userMigrate and emergencyWithdraw still work), so the flip must come after initiateMigration. This also compounds profile LOCAL-002: finalizeAndReset now calls mintDebt(), so an unhealthy hook additionally blocks the revival path - run setDispatcherHook(address(0)) before finalizeAndReset if in doubt.
original.possiblyIntentional: The single-recipient hook design is intentional; the un-documented interaction with a two-staker migration is the footgun (Law 3: non-obvious second-order consequence).

With growthBasisPoints == 0 (the repo's own test configuration) the deviation is EXACTLY ZERO. On the price-scaled models per-unit emission is independent of totalStaked (the audit M-03 fix), so staking freshly-minted units mid-loop gains nothing per unit; and on copy #4 the vector is additionally suppressed outright while Migrating. original.description: Handoff from the BatchNFTMinter code-scanner: an attacker-controlled recipient's onERC1155Received fires `count` times mid-batchMint and can re-enter the staker (stake / pullAndRefresh / claim -> _recomputeSchedule) at any chosen intermediate, settled price, rather than the end-of-batch price. VERDICT: REFUTED - the direction of the deviation is structurally wrong for an attacker, and it is fully self-correcting.

answersToPosedQuestions.q1_deviation_magnitude: rewardRate is exactly linear in latestPrice, so the deviation ratio is r^(k-count) where r = 1 + growthBasisPoints/1e4 and k is the chosen iteration. The bound is the first-iteration observation: 1 - r^-(count-1). Measured at gbp = 100 (1%) and count = 20: p_first 101e6 vs p_final 122.019e6, a maximum 1723 bps UNDER-size (rate 28,538,812,785,388 vs the honest 34,477,993,436,073). With the dispatcher's growthBasisPoints == 0 - the configuration used throughout the repo's own tests and the case CLAUDE.md describes as 'every staker earns exactly targetAPY' - the price does not move during a batch and the deviation is EXACTLY ZERO.
answersToPosedQuestions.q2_durable_over_earn: NO, in either direction. NFTMinterV2.sol:188 computes config.price = price + (price * growthBasisPoints)/10000 with an UNSIGNED growthBasisPoints, so within one batchMint the price is monotone NON-DECREASING. Every intermediate observation is therefore <= the end-of-batch price, and the attacker can only UNDER-size rewardRate - never over-size it. There is no route to over-earn. It is also self-correcting: the very next recompute by ANY user (stake/unstake/claim, all permissionless) restores the honest rate bit-for-bit (measured: 34,477,993,436,073 == the control rate exactly). And _updatePool always settles accrual at the OLD rate before the recompute, so nothing is re-priced retroactively.
answersToPosedQuestions.q3_materiality: Immaterial, and it back-fires. PoC test_ECON_I_midBatchIntermediatePriceCannotOverEarn: the attacker who pins the schedule at the first intermediate price earns 36.986 phUSD over the following 30 days versus 44.683 phUSD in the control that recomputes at the final price - i.e. the attacker pays 17.2% of their own yield for the privilege, having also paid for a full 20-mint batch. The residual is a pure griefing vector (the pool under-emits until the next recompute); the un-emitted budget stays in rewardBudget and recycles (see ECON-05's conservation proof), so nothing is lost, and any user can restore the rate for the cost of one claim(). Solvency (balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt) held exactly in both arms.
answersToPosedQuestions.q4_price_scaled_interaction: No new exposure. On the price-scaled models rate = totalStaked * latestPrice * priceScale * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR, so the PER-UNIT emission is latestPrice * priceScale * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR - independent of totalStaked. That is the audit M-03 fix, and it means an attacker who stakes freshly-minted units mid-loop to inflate totalStaked raises the aggregate rate strictly in proportion to the aggregate stake and gains nothing per unit. priceScale is a constant multiplier that scales both arms identically. On NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady specifically, the vector is additionally suppressed outright while poolState == Migrating, because _recomputeScheduleIfActive (L482) early-returns.

original.verdict: REFUTED. No finding. Recorded here so it is not re-derived on the next run. The only residual is a zero-profit, self-correcting under-emission grief whose cost to the attacker exceeds its cost to anyone else.

original.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.5: "**Duplicates** (`[USDC, USDC]`): both entries snapshot the same balance. The first transfer drains it; the second either reverts on insufficient balance or transfers into a now-empty pot. Either way it fails closed and harms only the caller. No dedupe pass" — read against §4.2: "The dispatcher donates reward token into this contract on every mint. Reading balances *before* the loop means the batcher is paid only the **prior accumulated pot**; the donations generated by their own batch stay behind to seed the next claimant... it is the only thing preventing a caller from **funding their own reward within a single transaction**."
original.actualBehavior: Duplicates do NOT fail closed in the configuration §4.2 itself assumes. The snapshot pass records `snapshot[i] = B` for every duplicate entry (B = pre-loop balance). The mint loop then increases the balance by the batch's OWN per-mint donation D (BalancerPoolerV2 at the pinned DISPATCHER_INDEX=4 forwards a `donationSplit`% USDC cut to `batchMinter` on every dispatch; primeToken is USDS, so USDC is a legal reward token and the §4.1 exclusion does not fire). The payout pass then transfers B once per entry against a balance of B+D. With k entries the caller extracts k*B whenever k*B <= B+D — i.e. the caller recaptures up to 100% of their own batch's donations. Empirically proven (workspace PoC, 2/2 passing): with B = 3e6 and D = 15e6, 2 duplicate entries pay the recipient 2*B and leave only D-B behind; 6 duplicate entries drain the contract to zero, paying the batcher `priorPot + all of its own donations`.
original.deviation: The story's own intent is unsafe, not merely mis-implemented. §4.5's stated justification for omitting a dedupe pass ("fails closed and harms only the caller") is factually false under §4.2's donating-dispatcher premise, and the resulting behaviour is precisely the "self-funded round-trip" that §4.2 declares load-bearing to prevent. The two sections of the same normative document contradict each other, and the implementation faithfully follows the wrong one. Cost to the attacker is zero marginal mints — the duplicate array is free relative to an honest single-entry claim, so this strictly dominates honest behaviour for every claimant, and the standing donate-forward pot degenerates to nothing.
original.impact: Protocol-funded incentive (SYA 30% USDC drip + BalancerPoolerV2 secondary cut) is recaptured by the batcher that generated it instead of seeding the next claimant. The donate-forward mechanic — the entire point of §4.2 — collapses. No user principal is at risk; this is a value leak of protocol-directed funds and a defeat of a documented invariant.
original.recommendation: Either (a) cap each payout at the live balance and skip on shortfall, (b) accumulate per-token amounts into a deduped payout map, or (c) re-read `balanceOf` at payout and pay `min(snapshot[i], balance)` while zeroing subsequent duplicate entries. Note (c) must NOT be implemented as a plain re-read — that is the §4.2 trap. Whichever is chosen, §4.5 must be rewritten and `test_DuplicateRewardTokenFailsClosed` must be re-armed with a donating dispatcher (see F-20-02).

And the ported NatSpec in src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:865-872: "DELTA vs `NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor`: ... `msg.sender` here is the MIGRATOR, so the `_safePay` form would route an existing staker's earned phUSD to the orchestrator while emitting `Claimed(user, ...)`. Only reachable when the deposit target already holds a position ... but wrong in every case."

original.actualBehavior: `NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor` still calls `pending = _safePay(pending);` at line 756, and `_safePay` delegates to `_safePayTo(msg.sender, ...)` (line 593-595). Under `onlyMigrator`, `msg.sender` is the migrator contract, so an existing staker's settled phUSD is transferred to the orchestrator while `Claimed(user, pending)` is emitted at line 757 naming the user. The staker's `committedDebt` is decremented as though the user was paid. Reachable via `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn` (src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:226) or `NFTStakerMigrator.migrate` (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:102) whenever the deposit target already holds a non-zero position — e.g. a parked user who re-staked directly between `finalizeAndReset` and `migrateIn`, or a user migrating into a staker they are already in. Recovery: `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.rescueERC20` (line 268) is an unconditional owner sweep so the funds are recoverable there; `NFTStakerMigrator` has NO rescue function at all (its only externals are `initiateMigration` and `migrate`), so phUSD routed to it is permanently stranded.

original.recommendation: Mirror the one-line fix into `src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:756` (`_safePayTo(user, pending)`). Report as a security finding, not a spec note — it is a live misdirection of user funds in an in-scope contract.

original.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.1: "**It is now an untrusted-input check on a value an attacker fully controls, and it is the thing standing between a caller and the payment-token balance held mid-transaction.** Two distinct failures it prevents: claiming the contract's payment-token balance (accumulated sub-threshold dust from prior batches) as 'reward'; ..." and §6 test 4: "`test_PaymentTokenDustNotClaimableAsReward`."
original.actualBehavior: The §4.1 guard is correctly and unconditionally implemented (src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:426-428), but its stated threat model overstates what it protects. Step 10's dust sweep (line 381-384) already transfers the contract's ENTIRE payment-token balance to `msg.sender` whenever it is >= DUST_THRESHOLD (1e6 wei — i.e. 1e-12 of an 18dp USDS), on a `count == 1` call with empty reward arrays, with no `nudgeSize` qualification required. Empirically proven (workspace PoC, PASS): a 500-USDS balance donated to the contract is swept in full to a non-qualifying caller, and `batchMint` returns `totalPaid == 0` while the caller is net positive. §4.1's narrow claim about SUB-threshold dust does hold (`remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD == 0` leaves it in place); the broader framing ("the thing standing between a caller and the payment-token balance") does not.
original.deviation: Spec-prose overstatement, not a code deviation. The sweep behaviour is pre-existing, contract-documented ("A griefer who pre-deposits payment-token to this contract simply donates to the next caller", src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:68) and explicitly preserved by §4.6, so the implementation is faithful; the normative doc's justification is what is wrong. The `totalPaid` floor-at-zero on a net-positive call is likewise pre-existing and §4.6-preserved, but it means the return value silently mis-reports the caller's true net spend.
original.recommendation: Correct §4.1's wording to scope the claim to sub-threshold dust and to the snapshot/refund-accounting perturbation. No code change required.

original.specText: commit 2bf13cb body: "drops ... the meaningless USDC != TOKEN_MINTER require"; script/DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:41-46: "The old 'nudge token == payment token' deploy guard is gone: that collision is now checked ON-CHAIN, per call, against every element of the caller's `rewardTokens` array (`BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken`)."
original.actualBehavior: The on-chain per-call check is NOT an equivalent replacement for the removed deploy-time assertion — it reverts the CALLER, it does not warn the OPERATOR. If `DISPATCHER_INDEX` is pointed at a dispatcher whose `primeToken()` equals the token the same dispatcher donates to `batchMinter`, the nudge is structurally dead: every attempt to claim it reverts `BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken`, and the accumulated pot is instead swept to whichever caller next runs a 1-mint batch (F-20-05). This is not hypothetical — `yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol` has `primeToken() == USDC` (line 189-191) AND donates USDC to `batchMinter` (line 340), and `NudgeRatchet.sol` likewise forwards USDC to `batchMinter` under a 6-decimal deploy guard. Only the currently-pinned `BalancerPoolerV2` (index 4, `primeToken` = USDS, donates USDC) is safe. The script's own NatSpec flags `DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4` as "ASSUMED ... the operator MUST confirm", so a repoint is an expected operation.
original.deviation: The removal of the deploy guard is faithful to the commit message, but the stated equivalence ("checked ON-CHAIN, per call") does not hold for the operator-facing failure mode the old guard existed to catch. Non-obvious owner footgun under Law 3: a competent, non-malicious operator repointing DISPATCHER_INDEX would be surprised that the nudge silently becomes unclaimable and leaks.
original.recommendation: Restore an operator-facing guard in the deploy script (and/or a `setDispatcherIndex` sanity log): resolve `configs(DISPATCHER_INDEX).dispatcher.primeToken()` and assert it differs from the intended reward asset for that dispatcher. Cheap, deploy-time only, and it restores the operator signal the on-chain check cannot give.

original.description: Between step 6 (`forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max)`) and step 8 (`forceApprove(nftMinter, 0)`) the contract holds a live unlimited payment-token approval, and the mint loop inside that window fires `onERC1155Received` on a fully caller-controlled `recipient`. The question is whether that callback can cause the minter to spend BatchNFTMinter's allowance. REFUTATION: `NFTMinterV2.mint` pulls with `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, config.dispatcher, price)` - the payer is always `msg.sender`, so a reentrant call from the recipient hook pays from the hook's own balance, not from BatchNFTMinter's allowance. The only other mint path, `mintFor`, is `authorizedMinters`-gated and moves no funds. Reentry back into `batchMint` itself is now blocked by the story-022 `nonReentrant`.
original.whyParked: Refuted against sibling-repo source rather than by a PoC, and the refutation depends on NFTMinterV2 keeping `msg.sender` as the payer. If NFTMinterV2 ever gains an arbitrary-`from` pull, this becomes live. Parked as a standing watch, not as a finding.

original.description: `_payRewards` makes an external call to a fully caller-supplied address (`IERC20(rewardTokens[i]).safeTransfer`), and `_snapshotRewards` calls `balanceOf` on the same. This is an arbitrary-code hook the caller controls, executing after the payment-token approval is revoked (step 8) but before the dust sweep (step 10). `nonReentrant` blocks reentry into `batchMint`; every other state-changing function is onlyOwner or onlyPauser; the snapshot pass is `view` so it cannot reenter at all. No exploitable sibling was identified. Residual surface worth a second pass: the callback fires while this contract still holds the un-swept payment-token residue, and while any in-flight dispatcher/hook state from the just-completed mint loop is settled but externally observable.

original.description: `rewardTokens` is deliberately NOT deduped (§4.5). A duplicate entry `[T, T]` snapshots the SAME pre-loop balance B twice, and both entries are paid out after the mint loop. The contract's own claim that the second transfer 'fails closed' is FALSE in the live configuration: the dispatcher donates reward token into this contract on EVERY mint (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch -> ISkyPSM.buyGem(batchMinter, gemAmt) delivers USDC straight to this contract), so the post-loop balance is B + D where D is THIS batch's own donations. The second transfer therefore succeeds whenever D >= B, paying the batcher their own batch's donations. That is exactly the self-funded round-trip that the §4.2 pre-loop snapshot exists to prevent and that the code calls 'load-bearing'. Repeating the token k times extracts k*B while the balance allows, and can drain the entire post-loop balance so that nothing is seeded forward for the next claimant.
missingMitigations: No dedupe of rewardTokens (explicitly declined as O(n^2))
No re-check that the cumulative payout for a token does not exceed its pre-loop snapshot
original.notes: Cheapest fix that keeps O(n): zero out `snapshot[j]` for any j whose token equals an already-paid token during the payout pass would still be O(n^2); alternatively cap the total transferred per token at the pre-loop balance by tracking a running `paidSoFar` against the snapshot, or simply assert post-loop that `balanceOf(this) >= D` was not consumed. Escalation check for the severity tier: the loss is the NEXT claimant's seed plus a rebate of the batcher's own donation, and it is repeatable.

original.description: Step 10 sweeps the ENTIRE residual payment-token balance to `msg.sender` with NO `nudgeSize` gate and no `qualifies` check. The payment token is DERIVED from `dispatcherIndex` at call time and `setDispatcherIndex` is owner-settable at any moment with no compatibility check against the contract's funding sources. If `dispatcherIndex` ever resolves to a dispatcher whose `primeToken()` is also one of this contract's funding tokens, the entire pot becomes (a) unclaimable through the nudge path, because the §4.1 exclusion reverts on listing it as a reward token, and (b) claimable in full by ANY caller with `count == 1`, through the ungated sweep. The concrete instantiation is live in the sibling repo: `NudgeRatchet.primeToken()` is USDC (6-decimal deploy guard) and `NudgeRatchet._dispatch` sweeps its full USDC balance to `batchMinter`, while `DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol` documents the PRIMARY funding path as a 30% USDC drip (`StableYieldAccumulator.setNudgeAddress(<this>)`) into this same contract. Under the intended `DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4` (BalancerPoolerV2, prime token USDS) the configuration is safe; a repoint to the ratchet index inverts it. The deploy script's `require`s check only that `DISPATCHER_INDEX != 0` and the story-022 change explicitly REMOVED the old deploy-time 'nudge token == payment token' guard, replacing it with a per-call revert that protects only the nudge path and does nothing about the sweep path.
missingMitigations: Sweep is not bounded by the caller's own unspent `paymentAmount` (it sweeps third-party/dripped balances too)
No invariant tying `dispatcherIndex`'s primeToken to the set of funding tokens
Deploy-time collision guard was removed, and the replacement per-call guard does not cover the sweep
`setDispatcherIndex` has no re-validation of the funding configuration
original.notes: Law 3 footgun test: a competent, non-malicious owner repointing `dispatcherIndex` to the USDC-primed NudgeRatchet would be SURPRISED that the nudge pot becomes both unclaimable and free-for-all, and that (if this contract is also the ratchet's `batchMinter`) mint payments round-trip back into this contract and are refunded by the same sweep, making batched mints effectively free while mint-debt still accrues. In-scope hazard, not owner-malice. Even in the safe USDS configuration the sweep hands any stranded/donated payment token to the first `count == 1` caller with no gate; that narrower reading is documented ('a griefer who pre-deposits payment-token simply donates to the next caller') and is parked at MR-BNM-08.

original.description: `stake` (617), `unstake` (645), `claim` (666) and `emergencyWithdraw` (735) carry no `poolState` gate, so they stay open while the pool is `Migrating`. Two consequences specific to the PRICE-SCALED model, where `R = totalStaked * latestPrice * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR` depends on `totalStaked`: (1) a permissionless `stake(1)` during `Migrating` re-populates `totalStaked` while the tail `_recomputeScheduleIfActive()` deliberately no-ops, so the frozen snapshot's `rewardRate` no longer corresponds to the live pool, and any caller can indefinitely block `finalizeAndReset` (which requires `totalStaked == 0`) for one ERC1155 unit; (2) an unstake/emergencyWithdraw during `Migrating` shrinks `totalStaked` without re-sizing R for the same reason. Accrual itself is safe (`_updatePool` early-returns while `Migrating`), so this is availability/state-consistency rather than over-emission.
missingMitigations: No auto-pause on `initiateMigration` (the freeze relies on the operator separately pausing)
`finalizeAndReset`'s `totalStaked == 0` precondition is griefable by any staker

original.description: The payout amount is a balance SNAPSHOT taken before the mint loop and transferred verbatim afterwards; `minRewards` is a floor on the contract's pre-transfer balance, not on what `recipient` actually receives. Two skews follow. (a) Fee-on-transfer: the delivered amount is below the declared floor, so `minRewards` does not do what a caller reading it as slippage protection would assume - explicitly documented as caller-discretion. (b) NEGATIVE-REBASING or otherwise shrinking token: if the balance falls between the snapshot and the payout, `safeTransfer(snapshot[i])` reverts and the WHOLE batch (all mints, all other reward tokens) rolls back - a one-token DoS on the entire batch. The token set here is fully permissionless, which is exactly the condition under which this pattern's `notVulnerableWhen` ('token set restricted to known non-fee, non-rebasing tokens') does not hold; the mitigating factor is that the caller selects the tokens and only harms themselves.
missingMitigations: No balanceAfter - balanceBefore measurement on the payout leg
Snapshot amount is not clamped to `min(snapshot[i], currentBalance)` at payout time
original.notes: Clamping the payout to `min(snapshot[i], balanceOf(this))` would also close PATTERN-001's second-transfer window and remove this revert-DoS in one change. Note the two findings pull in the same direction, so a fix should be evaluated jointly.

dispositions.reason: Tool noise — Slither `reentrancy-no-eth` across the staker/migrator family. Adjudicated by code-scanner (46 static entries reviewed on these files, 1 real, 45 noise) on three collapsing facts: (a) EVERY non-owner state-changing entrypoint on the changed files carries `nonReentrant`, and every other entrypoint is onlyOwner, onlyPauser or onlyMigrator; (b) `stakedToken` and `rewardToken` are IMMUTABLE first-party contracts (NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:115-116), so the 'no transfer hooks' trust assumption cannot be broken by a later owner rotation, which closes every transfer-before-accounting surface in `_safePayTo`; (c) ERC1155 `safeTransferFrom` invokes `onERC1155Received` on the RECIPIENT only — every entry citing an INBOUND transfer (..., address(this), ...) as an attacker-control point is MIS-MODELLED, since control goes to the staker's own inert ERC1155Holder, never to the sender. Specific adjudications: SAST-007 (initiateMigration) — the transient inconsistency is that pull() raised balance before rewardBudget was resized, i.e. transiently OVER-collateralised, a conservative direction with nothing extractable; SAST-010 (depositFor) — a genuine transfer-then-account ordering inside _safePayTo, inert because rewardToken is immutable first-party phUSD with no hooks and the function is nonReentrant onlyMigrator. The single entry in this cluster adjudicated REAL is SAST-008, which is MERGED into DEDUP-20-016 rather than dropped.

Specific adjudications: SAST-007 (initiateMigration) — the transient inconsistency is that pull() raised balance before rewardBudget was resized, i.e. transiently OVER-collateralised, a conservative direction with nothing extractable; SAST-010 (depositFor) — a genuine transfer-then-account ordering inside _safePayTo, inert because rewardToken is immutable first-party phUSD with no hooks and the function is nonReentrant onlyMigrator. The single entry in this cluster adjudicated REAL is SAST-008, which is MERGED into DEDUP-20-016 rather than dropped.

dispositions.reason: D-21 REFUTED WITH SOURCE. NFTMinterV2._executeMint either reverts on its four require()s or returns an unconditional `true` (lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft/src/NFTMinterV2.sol:200). NO path returns false, so a caller can never be charged for `count` and receive fewer. Even against a hypothetical false-returning minter the caller is not over-charged: unspent budget is returned by the step-10 sweep and totalPaid floors at 0. The residual 'silent-no-op minter' scenario is reachable only via an owner-set broken tokenMinter — an OBVIOUS misconfiguration, suppressed under Law 3. Adjudicated by code-scanner CODE-BM20-104. The free QA hardening it recommends is preserved in qaHardeningCandidates so the recommendation is not lost with the refutation.

That advice is REJECTED AS ACTIVELY HARMFUL: adopting it on `batchMigrate` would be a REGRESSION — silently skipping a user mid-migration STRANDS that user's position while the batch reports success. The loop reverting is the correct FAIL-CLOSED behaviour here. This is exactly the shape of 'obvious fix that strands funds' this project has been bitten by before, so it is written down rather than left to be re-suggested next run. The underlying dust-revert concern is profile LOCAL-007 (remedy: a 1-wei topUp) and the batch is idempotent and re-runnable.

original.description: Function returns a value but it is ignored. Consider checking the return value.

dispositions.reason: Tool noise — `uninitialized-local`. Every cited declaration is a loop accumulator or index, written via `+=` / `++` before any meaningful read and deterministically zero-initialised by Solidity value-type semantics. Verified line by line. DUAL-CORROBORATION CAVEAT recorded: Slither and Aderyn agreeing adds NO independent weight here — both implement the same syntactic 'declared without initialiser' rule, so the agreement is correlated by construction and was not treated as confirmation.

original.description: Initialize all the variables. If a variable is meant to be initialized to zero, explicitly set it to zero to improve code readability.
